(a) State the nature of an asteroid. [1]
(b) State the position of the asteroid belt in the solar system. [1]

E2.text_clean:
E2. This question is about the properties of a star.
(a) The peak in the radiation spectrum of a star X is at a wavelength of 300 nm.
Show that the surface temperature of star X is about 10 000 K. [2]
(b) (i) The radius of star X is $4.5R_S$ where $R_S$ is the radius of the Sun. The surface temperature of the Sun is $5.7\times10^{3}$ K.
Determine the ratio $\frac{\text{luminosity of star X}}{\text{luminosity of the Sun}}$. [3]
(ii) Calculate, assuming that the power in the mass–luminosity relationship is 3.5, the ratio $\frac{\text{mass of star X}}{\text{mass of Sun}}$. [3]
(c) On the Hertzsprung–Russell diagram, label
(i) the position of star X with the letter X. [1]
(ii) the position of the Sun with the letter S. [1]
[Graph: blank Hertzsprung–Russell grid; vertical axis relative luminosity (Sun = 1) on log scale from 0.01 to 1000; horizontal axis surface temperature / K from 40 000 to 2500 (decreasing, log scale, marks 40 000, 20 000, 10 000, 5000, 2500)]
(d) Explain, with reference to the Chandrasekhar limit, whether or not star X will become a white dwarf. [2]

E3.text_clean:
E3. This question is about variable stars.
Cepheid variable stars are used as "standard candles" by astronomers.
(a) (i) State what is meant by a standard candle. [1]
(ii) Outline the properties of a Cepheid star that allow it to be used as a standard candle. [2]
(b) Explain how astronomers use their observations of a Cepheid star to determine the distance from the star to Earth. [3]

E4. This question is about Newton's model of the universe.

For each of Newton's three suggestions, outline one piece of current astronomical evidence that contradicts the suggestion. [3]
Infinite: ...
Uniform: ...
Static: ...

E5.text_clean:
E5. This question is about red-shift.
The wavelengths of radio signals from galaxy A are found to be red-shifted from the wavelengths that would be observed from sources at rest relative to Earth.
(a) The fractional change in wavelength of the radio signals from galaxy A is $9.4\times10^{-3}$.
Calculate, in $\text{km s}^{-1}$, the average velocity of galaxy A relative to Earth. [2]
(b) A supernova was observed within galaxy A. At the peak of its emissions, the supernova had an absolute magnitude of –20 and an apparent magnitude of 13.
Show that the distance from Earth to the supernova is about 40 Mpc. [3]
(c) Estimate, using your answer to (a) and the result for (b), the age of the universe. ($1\text{ pc} = 3.1\times10^{13}$ km) [2]

F1.text_clean:
F1. This question is about amplitude modulation.
The graph shows the power spectrum of a carrier wave that has been amplitude modulated by a single-frequency information signal.
[Graph: intensity against frequency / MHz, axis from 149.999 to 150.001; a tall line at 150.000 MHz and two shorter side lines symmetrically placed at about 149.9994 and 150.0006 MHz]
(a) State the
(i) frequency of the information signal. [1]
(ii) bandwidth of the modulated signal. [1]
(b) Frequency modulated (FM) radio transmission is preferred to amplitude modulated (AM) radio transmission when high audio quality is required. Explain, with reference to the amplitude of the frequency modulated signal, why this is true. [3]
(c) Outline two disadvantages in the use of FM transmission compared to AM transmission. [2]

(a) Identify the blocks A, B and C. [2]
A: ...

The signal is sampled every 1.0 ms, beginning at a sampling time $t = 0.0$ ms.
[Graph: analogue input voltage / V (from –10 to about 7.5) and digital output equivalent (000 to 111) against time / ms from 0 to 6; the signal rises to about 3.8 V, peaks near 7.3 V at 1.5 ms, falls below zero after 3 ms, minimum about –7.5 V near 4.7 ms]

F3.text_clean:
F3. This question is about an optic fibre.
Monochromatic light enters an optic fibre, from air, along direction A that is at an angle $\theta$ to the axis of the fibre.
[Diagram: optic fibre with core between two cladding layers; ray A incident on the end face of the core at angle $\theta$ to the fibre axis]
The refractive index of the core is 1.62 and the refractive index of the cladding is 1.52. The critical angle at the core-cladding boundary is 70°.
(a) Calculate the greatest angle of incidence $\theta$ that can be used with this fibre. [3]
(b) Sketch the path of the light in the core on the diagram above. [2]
(c) Information is transmitted along the fibre in the form of pulsed light. Two rays of this light enter the core at the same instant as shown in the diagram below.
[Diagram: fibre core and cladding; ray 1 enters along the axis, ray 2 enters at an angle]
Discuss the effect of modal dispersion on the subsequent transmission of the information along the fibre. [3]
(d) Outline two advantages in the use of optic fibres over coaxial metal cables for the transmission of data between continents. [2]

F4.text_clean:
F4. This question is about the operational amplifier (op-amp).
(a) State two properties of an ideal operational amplifier (op-amp). [2]
(b) An operational amplifier circuit is designed to switch on a warning buzzer when the potential difference (pd) at point A drops below a voltage V. P is connected to the supply rails via resistances of 50 kΩ and 100 kΩ. The warning buzzer sounds when the pd across it is 30 V.
[Circuit: 50 kΩ and 100 kΩ resistors in series between +15 V and –15 V rails; their junction connects to A, to the non-inverting input Q (+) and to the inverting input P (–) of an op-amp; the op-amp output R connects through a buzzer to the +15 V rail]
(i) Show that the voltage at P is +5 V. [2]
(ii) State the value of V. [1]
(iii) Explain why the buzzer will switch on when point A drops below voltage V. [3]

G1.text_clean:
G1. This question is about light and optical instruments.
A thin converging glass lens has focal length $f = 0.20$ m.
(a) An object is placed 0.10 m in front of the lens.
(i) On the diagram, construct rays to locate the image of the object, O. The focal points of the lens are labelled F. [3]
[Diagram: converging lens on a principal axis with focal points F on each side; object arrow O between the left F and the lens]
(ii) Explain whether the image in (a)(i) is real or virtual. [1]
(b) The object in (a) is now moved so that it is located 0.40 m from the lens. Calculate
(i) the distance of the image from the lens. [2]
(ii) the linear magnification. [2]
(c) State typical wavelengths in a vacuum for
(i) blue light. [1]
(ii) red light. [1]
(d) The refractive index of the glass in the lens is greater for blue wavelengths than for red wavelengths.
The diagram shows two rays of blue light incident on the lens.
[Diagram: two parallel rays of blue light refracted by a converging lens to meet at a point on the principal axis]
On the diagram, sketch the paths of the rays if red light is used instead of blue light. [1]

(i) monochromatic. [1]
(ii) coherent. [2]

G3.text_clean:
G3. This question is about X-ray production and diffraction.
(a) Outline how X-rays are used to determine the atomic spacing in a crystal. [3]
(b) Electrons are incident on the target of an X-ray tube after acceleration through a potential difference of 15 kV. Calculate the minimum wavelength of X-rays produced by the X-ray tube. [2]

G4.text_clean:
G4. This question is about thin-film interference.
The anti-reflective coating of a lens consists of a thin layer of a suitable material placed between the air and the glass of the lens.
[Diagram: ray incident at angle $\theta$ to the normal on an air–coating–glass layer; reflected rays from the air-coating and coating-glass boundaries]
The following data are available.
Refractive index of air = 1.0
Refractive index of coating = 1.2
Refractive index of glass = 1.5
(a) State what phase change occurs on reflection at the air-coating boundary and at the coating-glass boundary. [1]
(b) The thickness d of the coating layer is 110 nm.
Determine the wavelength for which there is no resultant reflection from the surface of the lens for light at normal incidence ($\theta = 0°$). [3]

H1.text_clean:
H1. This question is about relativistic kinematics.
Speedy is in a spacecraft being chased by Police Officer Sylvester. In Officer Sylvester's frame of reference, Speedy is moving directly towards Officer Sylvester at 0.25c.
[Diagram: Police Officer Sylvester's spacecraft (with two flashing lamps) behind Speedy's spacecraft, arrow between them]
(a) Describe what is meant by a frame of reference. [2]
(b) Officer Sylvester switches on the blue flashing lamps on his police spacecraft.
(i) Calculate, assuming that a Galilean transformation applies to this situation, the value of the speed of the light that Speedy would measure using the flashing lamps. [1]
(ii) Speedy measures the speed of the light emitted by the flashing lamps. Deduce, using the relativistic addition of velocities, that Speedy will obtain a value for the speed of light equal to c. [3]
(c) At a later time the police spacecraft is alongside Speedy's spacecraft. The police spacecraft is overtaking Speedy's spacecraft at a constant velocity.
Officer Sylvester is at a point midway between the flashing lamps, both of which he can see. At the instant when Officer Sylvester and Speedy are opposite each other, Speedy observes that the blue lamps flash simultaneously.
[Diagram: Speedy's spacecraft alongside the police spacecraft; back lamp and front lamp on the police spacecraft with Officer Sylvester midway between them, opposite Speedy]
State and explain which lamp is observed to flash first by Officer Sylvester. [4]
(d) The police spacecraft is travelling at a constant speed of 0.5c relative to Speedy's frame of reference. The light from a flash of one of the lamps travels across the police spacecraft and is reflected back to the light source. Officer Sylvester measures the time taken for the light to return to the source as $1.2\times10^{-8}$ s.
(i) Outline why the time interval measured by Officer Sylvester is a proper time interval. [1]
(ii) Determine, as observed by Speedy, the time taken for the light to travel across the police spacecraft and back to its source. [3]

The capsule now starts to decelerate.

(b) Outline, with reference to the principle of equivalence, how the situation in (a) relates to the concept of gravitational red-shift. [2]

H4.text_clean:

H5.text_clean:

Calculate the minimum density required for Sirius B to become a black hole in the future. [2]

I2.text_clean:
I2. This question is about the use of X-rays and ultrasound in medical imaging.
(a) The diagram below shows X-rays being used to scan a sample of bone and muscle.
[Diagram: X-ray tube above adjacent blocks of muscle and bone, each of thickness x, resting on a photographic plate]
(i) Outline how the arrangement differentiates between bone and muscle. [2]
(ii) Use the data below to determine the ratio $\frac{I_b}{I_m}$ where $I_b$ and $I_m$ are the intensity of X-rays reaching the photographic plate through the bone and the muscle, respectively. [3]
Thickness x of sample = 10.0 cm
Linear attenuation coefficient of bone $\mu_b$ = 0.53 cm$^{-1}$
Linear attenuation coefficient of muscle $\mu_m$ = 0.30 cm$^{-1}$
(iii) The half-value thickness of a material increases as the energy of the radiation increases.

(c) An isotope of technetium used in medicine has a physical half-life of 6 hours.
(i) Define effective half-life. [2]
